rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store. Any file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build.
rules.evidence: app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:14-29 walks every .dart file under lib/, skips lib/spine/, and fails on an import OR export of sqflite|drift|hive|hive_flutter|shared_preferences|sqlite3|sqlite3_flutter_libs|idb_shim|idb_sqflite|sembast|isar|objectbox|realm in either quote style, plus dart:indexed_db and dart:html (regex at :8-11); a second test (:31-41) confines drivers to lib/spine/store/. Only two files in the tree import a driver: app/lib/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10 (package:sqlite3) and app/lib/spine/store/store_web.dart:4 (package:idb_shim). There is one persistence interface, app/lib/spine/store/store.dart:16-41, and it carries events, blobs AND key/value meta, so nothing else needs a store: the pairing key and peer address (app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:141-142, :280), the notification preferences (app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:54), the composer draft (app/lib/regions/chat/chat_region.dart:289) and the device id (app/lib/transport/local/local_transport.dart:51-54) all go through spine.meta/setMeta (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:366-367). Only one file outside lib/spine/ writes to disk at all, app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:23-27, and it writes a content-hash-named copy of a blob already in the spine into getTemporaryDirectory() so video_player and the OS picker can be handed a path — a cache, not a store. One gap in ENFORCEMENT rather than in the code: the scan is Directory('lib') (persistence_boundary_test.dart:22), so app/tool/ and app/test/ are outside it. app/tool/host_daemon.dart:33 imports package:desk/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart — the spine's own store, not a driver — so nothing offends today, but a driver imported from app/tool/ would not fail the build.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, with docs/EVENT_TYPES.md and the code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list.
rules.evidence: Eighteen types in app/lib/spine/types.dart:85-242, eighteen numbered rows in docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:33-50, and app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18 asserts the documented list EQUALS the registry list in order, asserts >= 14 (:16) and asserts no duplicates (:17). Thread rendering: every spec names a renderer, and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30 holds both directions against kThreadRenderers (app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:338-356) — every named renderer exists, every renderer is named. Search behaviour comes off the registry rather than a switch: app/lib/spine/search.dart:51 honours spec.search.excluded, :39-43 indexes spec.search.textFields, :46-48 the facets. Notification treatment comes off the registry for defaults: app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:41-52 builds the per-type defaults from t.notify. THREE SHORTFALLS. (a) The person-facing notification label is a SECOND hand-maintained list, app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:85-104, and it has seventeen arms for eighteen types — 'passed_on' is missing, so the fallback at :103 (_ => type.replaceAll('_',' ')) puts the row 'passed on' in the notification settings (rendered at :137, and passed_on qualifies for a row because its notify is Notify.quiet, types.dart:222). Nothing tests _said; thread_types_test.dart:32-52 guards only summaryOf. (b) The doc and the code agree on names and order only — spine_schema_test.dart:10 matches the type id and stops at the second column, so the payload columns have drifted: docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:34,35,36 list no 'mime' for photo, video or voice_note while types.dart:98,110,120 all carry it as optional. (c) types.dart:1 says 'the same seventeen types' over a list of eighteen.

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line. Check the registry and check that the commit which added the fourth module touched nothing under the first three.
rules.evidence: The registry half is real. app/lib/modules/registry.dart:10-16 is five const entries; app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:40-52 iterates kModules with no per-module branch, and app/lib/capture/hooks.dart:401 does the same, so a new module reaches Us and the capture harness without either file changing. app/lib/modules/module.dart:31-77 hands a module only the log, the two people, the clock and one emit — it cannot open a store, so its history cannot drift from the couple's. app/lib/modules/shelf/shelf_module.dart:12-19 imports nothing from another module. app/test/floors_test.dart:108-118 holds >= 4 modules with unique ids, each declaring event types that exist in the one log. BUT the fifth module in the tree, shelf, is not a directory plus one line: 'passed_on' also had to be added to app/lib/spine/types.dart:218-225, to kThreadRenderers as 'shelf_card' (app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:355), to stockForType (app/lib/material/assignment.dart:31), to docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:48, and to the hand-written map in app/test/one_kind_of_paper_per_kind_of_event_test.dart:17-23 — and the one place it was NOT added, app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:85-104, is the visible defect in rule 2. Six files plus the line, not one line; the claim in registry.dart:1-2 and module.dart:4-5 is true only for a module that reuses an existing event type. A residual per-id switch also survives at us_region.dart:63-68, though its default (_ => 2) means a sixth module works without touching it. The commit-level half of this rule I could not perform: this review is run without build history and I did not open the log.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events. They must not reach the log.
rules.evidence: They are a different type on the wire. app/lib/transport/transport.dart:131-147 defines Ephemeral (kind/from/at/data) as explicitly 'a frame that is not an event', and PullResponse.ephemeral (:127-129) is documented 'Never stored'. app/lib/scope.dart:174-179 is the only typing sender and it calls transport.sendEphemeral, never emit; app/lib/scope.dart:153-166 consumes an inbound typing frame into a bool and a six-second Timer that expires on its own; the one path into the log is scope.emit at :171-172, which is spine.append. Nothing anywhere calls append or emit with 'typing' or 'presence' (grep over app/lib returns only the ephemeral path and the UI string in app/lib/voice/strings.dart:26). Asserted twice: app/test/transport_local_test.dart:207-222 sends a typing frame client-to-host and a presence frame host-to-client, sees both delivered, and then asserts r.host.length == 0 and r.client.length == 0; app/test/reliability_test.dart:116-129 measures host.length + client.length before and after a typing frame and records the capability only if the frame arrived AND neither log grew.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread.
rules.evidence: Three independent guards. The projection returns before ever adding a row: app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:272-278 folds read_marker into _readUpto and returns, and the generic line at :280 (if (!spec.rowInThread) return;) catches every type the registry marks that way, so the rule is the registry's answer rather than a special case. The registry says so: app/lib/spine/types.dart:153-161 (rowInThread: false, renderer 'ink_dries'), and 'ink_dries' maps to _neverARow at app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:347. And the golden replay asserts it on real output: app/test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart:56 expects thread.items to contain no read_marker after a log that includes one (:119); app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:31-34 and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:96-104 hold the flag itself.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file, history included.
rules.evidence: I enumerated every object reachable from every ref (114 commits, 3973 distinct objects from git rev-list --all --objects), took the 1293 that are text blobs under 2 MB, and grepped each for tskey-[A-Za-z0-9], BEGIN <...> PRIVATE KEY, BEGIN OPENSSH, an assigned TS_AUTHKEY, an assigned pairing_secret, AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16} and ghp_ tokens. Nine matches, all of them the literal placeholder with an ellipsis — 'TS_AUTHKEY=tskey-auth-…' — in tools/tailscale/up.sh, docs/PHONES.md and app/test/reliability_test.dart:337. No real key, in the working tree or behind it. The exclusions are in place: .gitignore:11-15 covers .env, *.authkey and /toolchain/ts/, and the vendored toolchain (the only place the string 'authkey' otherwise appears, in Blender's bundled CPython multiprocessing) is itself ignored at .gitignore:2. Structurally there is nothing to leak: the pairing secret is six words spoken once (app/lib/transport/protocol/wire.dart:43-46), never written down — derivePairingKey (:67-71) HKDFs them with the host id and only the derived 32 bytes are kept, in the spine's own meta table (app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:142), not in a file.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key.
rules.evidence:
The binding half is strong. app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:22-33 accepts 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 and nothing else; addressToServeOn (:56-71) refuses a declared address that is not one and throws NotOnTheTailnet rather than falling back when no tailnet interface exists. There is no wildcard bind anywhere: app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:50-53 binds InternetAddress(bind.address) and the only two producers of that address are app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:72-79 and the loopback local transport. app/test/tailnet_test.dart:11-43 covers 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 192.168/10.x, both edges of the /10, '::', fe80::, the empty string, and asserts a declared bad address throws. The auth half is sound where it applies: server_io.dart:87-93 reads the body, parses Authorization, and 401s with no body unless _authenticated (:119-130) passes — right client device id, timestamp within kAuthSkew (5 minutes, wire.dart:11), HMAC-SHA256 over method
path
ts
nonce
sha256(body) (wire.dart:83-87) compared in constant time (:89-96), and a nonce not seen before (NonceCache, :128-143). THREE GAPS. (a) server_io.dart:80-83 sends every non-/v1 request to _serveStatic (:267-292), which serves the PWA bundle to anyone on the tailnet with no signature at all — so the invariant the file states in its own header (':2-3, every request except the two pairing calls must carry a valid pairing signature') is not what the code does. It leaks the app shell, not couple data, and I checked the traversal: Uri.parse removes dot segments and does not decode %2F, so p.normalize + the '..' guard at :274-278 keeps p.join under pwaRoot for '///etc/passwd', '//../etc/passwd', '/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd' and '/%2Fetc%2Fpasswd'. (b) Nothing tests a forged signature: app/test/transport_local_test.dart:70-86 is named 'unauthenticated requests are refused' but the only refusal it exercises is pulling before pairing (:72-73), so a wrong-key MAC, a stale timestamp and a replayed nonce are all unexercised. (c) The one end-to-end tailnet run recorded in evidence/reliability.json bound host_listener 127.0.0.1:8443, because a userspace tailscaled has no TUN (tailscale_transport.dart:77 makes the substitution explicit); that is narrower than a phone, not wider, but it means the tailnet-address bind is only ever unit-tested. Minor: the unauthenticated nonce endpoint (server_io.dart:139-149) adds to a _pairNonces set (:44) that has no cap and no expiry while the ten-minute window is open.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font was downloaded from the internet.
rules.evidence: 665 files under assets/ excluding the manifest itself; I matched them against the 674 keys of assets/MANIFEST.json.files and 663 have an entry, every entry carries a non-empty 'generator' and most carry the full settings dict. The two without one are assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json and assets/tears/relief.json — generator index sidecars, exempted by name at tools/check/manifest.py:22-23; running the checker prints '661 files in assets/, 0 without an entry naming their generator' and exits 0. Every generator is a script in this repository: blender/folds/fold.py (245 files), blender/paper/tear_relief.py (113), blender/objects/objects.py (108), tools/tears/tear.py (57), blender/paper/stocks.py (54), blender/bits/bits.py (44), tools/sound/synth.py (44), tools/handwriting/build.py (5), tools/ink_plate.py (2), blender/shell/desk.py (2). Nothing fetches: grepping tools/ and blender/ for urllib, requests, urlopen, curl, wget and http(s):// returns only tools/apt-prereqs.sh:8 (an apt package list), tools/push/webpush.py:196 (a push.example.net string in a self-test) and tools/capture/android.sh:15-16 (127.0.0.1). The two fonts are built from strokes, not downloaded — tools/handwriting/build.py:11 'Nothing is downloaded', and assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json records 155 glyphs per face with the full pen and jitter parameters. Minor: assets/MANIFEST.json still carries 11 entries for PNGs written to a scratch directory outside the repository, and tools/check/manifest.py:59 deliberately excludes '../' keys from the stale report rather than dropping them (the --fill path at :61-73 would).

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to.
rules.evidence: flutter test is green: 103 tests, 'All tests passed!', exit 0. Most of the suite is unusually honest — several tests read the source and fail the build on a pattern (persistence_boundary_test.dart, nothing_moves_on_the_wall_clock_test.dart:50-69, capture_hooks_return_test.dart:35-60, one_kind_of_paper_per_kind_of_event_test.dart:26-38), and nothing_is_drawn_by_the_diagnostic_test.dart:45-57 resolves the actual DefaultTextStyle the framework gave each Text rather than asserting a widget exists. FOUR PLACES WHERE THE NAME IS STRONGER THAN THE ASSERTION. (a) app/test/reliability_test.dart:296-345: when the two tailnet nodes are not answering the test records 'pending' into evidence/reliability.json and returns at :345 without executing a single expect — a green test that checked nothing, under a name that says it checked the tailscale transport. It is recorded honestly in the artifact, but the suite result does not distinguish the two outcomes. (b) app/test/tailnet_test.dart:45-62 branches on whether the machine happens to have a tailnet interface and passes down either arm. (c) app/test/transport_local_test.dart:70 claims 'unauthenticated requests are refused' and exercises only the not-yet-paired case (see rule 7). (d) app/test/one_kind_of_paper_per_kind_of_event_test.dart:17-23 is a hand-maintained file-to-type map, so a sixth module that forgets to add itself is silently unchecked by the test whose whole purpose is catching that. And one thing no test covers at all: app/pubspec.yaml:97-99 declares the font family DeskStamp with asset assets/fonts/TeoHand.ttf, i.e. DeskStamp is Teo's handwriting. tools/handwriting/build.py:40 builds three faces including DeskStamp, but assets/fonts/ holds only NoorHand.ttf and TeoHand.ttf and assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json records only two faces, so the third was never produced. Hands.stamp (app/lib/material/hands.dart:32-38), Hands.onDesk (:47-52) and Hands.margin (:55-60) therefore all resolve to the same file as Hands.teo (:23-29).

findings.where: the font declaration block, and app/lib/material/hands.dart:32-60
findings.what: The family DeskStamp is declared with asset assets/fonts/TeoHand.ttf, so the app's furniture register — tabs, stamps, module labels, dates, kinds, margin notes — is set in one of the two people's handwriting; tools/handwriting/build.py:40 lists DeskStamp among the faces it builds but assets/fonts/ contains only NoorHand.ttf and TeoHand.ttf and assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json records only those two faces.
findings.why: The type system claims four registers and delivers two: Hands.stamp, Hands.onDesk and Hands.margin all resolve to the same TTF as Hands.teo, so the design system is internally incoherent in exactly the way the coherence row is about — the same thing is not the same thing everywhere, and one person's hand is doing the app's impersonal speaking.

findings.where: the _said switch that labels each event type in the notification settings
findings.what: _said has seventeen arms for eighteen registry types: passed_on is missing, so its row (rendered at :137, and it qualifies because types.dart:222 gives it Notify.quiet) is labelled by the fallback at :103 as 'passed on' — the registry id with its underscore replaced.
findings.why: Rule 2 requires a notification treatment per type, and this is a second per-type list that the registry does not drive and no test holds; it is the same failure app/lib/spine/types.dart:6-10 and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:32-52 were written to eliminate for summaryOf, reappearing one file over as the fifth module's type was added everywhere else and missed here.

findings.where: the comment claiming a module is a directory plus one line
findings.what: The fifth module in the tree needed six files besides its own directory and its registry line — app/lib/spine/types.dart:218-225, app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:355, app/lib/material/assignment.dart:31, docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:48, app/test/one_kind_of_paper_per_kind_of_event_test.dart:22 and (missed) app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:85 — because it brought a new event type with it.
findings.why: The rule is the brief's extensibility test, and the registry genuinely carries the Us surface and the capture harness without change; but a shared-life module almost by definition brings its own kind of event, so the claim as stated overstates what adding one costs, and the one place the checklist was not followed is now a visible defect.

findings.what: Every non-/v1 request bypasses _authenticated entirely and is served from pwaRoot with no pairing signature, contradicting the file's own stated invariant at :2-3 that every request except the two pairing calls must carry one; the pairing-nonce set at :44 also has no cap or expiry while the ten-minute window is open.
findings.why: Rule 7 says the host refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key; the exception is defensible (the PWA has to be fetched before pairing) and I verified it cannot be walked out of pwaRoot, but it is undocumented in the place that documents the opposite, and no test covers the static route or a forged signature.

findings.where: the tailscale reliability test's early return when the nodes are not answering
findings.what: The test writes a 'pending' block into evidence/reliability.json and returns without executing any expect, so it is green whether or not anything over the tailnet was ever checked.
findings.why: Rule 9 asks that a test assert what its name says; the artifact records the distinction honestly, but the suite result does not, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:45-62 has the same pass-either-way shape.

findings.what: The regex at :10 compares only the numbered type id, so the doc's payload column has drifted from the code: photo, video and voice_note all carry an optional 'mime' in app/lib/spine/types.dart:98, :110 and :120 that the doc does not list; app/lib/spine/types.dart:1 also still says 'seventeen types' over a list of eighteen.
findings.why: Rule 2 requires docs/EVENT_TYPES.md and the code to agree; they agree on the list and not yet on the contents, and the test that is supposed to keep them together only holds the names.

findings.where: the directory the driver scan walks
findings.what: The scan is Directory('lib'), so app/tool/ and app/test/ are outside the rule; nothing offends today (app/tool/host_daemon.dart:33 imports the spine's own store_sqlite.dart, not package:sqlite3) but a driver imported from a headless tool would not fail the build.
findings.why: Rule 1 says any file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build, and app/tool/ is such a file's most likely home — it is the one process that opens a store without the app around it.

what_is_working: One log, one store, one interface: app/lib/spine/store/store.dart:16-41 carries events, blobs and key/value meta together, so the pairing key, the notification preferences, the composer draft and the device id all live in the spine and there is nothing for a second store to be for. The rule is enforced by a test that fails the build (app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart), and it covers exports and both quote styles rather than the obvious import.

The event registry actually drives the app rather than describing it. app/lib/spine/types.dart:85-242 is read by the thread projection (thread.dart:280), the search index (search.dart:39-51), the notification defaults (notifications.dart:41-52) and the renderer table, and app/test/thread_types_test.dart holds both ends in four directions — every renderer named exists, every renderer is reachable, every type reads as a sentence rather than an id, and marginality is asked of the registry rather than of a second list.

Typing and presence are a different kind of thing on the wire, not a filtered event: Ephemeral (transport.dart:131-147) with its own channel, and two independent tests that assert both logs stay the same length while the frame is delivered.

The binding rule is treated as the load-bearing line it is: 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 only, a declared address checked rather than trusted, an exception rather than a fallback when there is no tailnet, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:11-43 shooting at every address a mistake would reach for.

The signing scheme is properly built: HMAC-SHA256 over method, path, timestamp, nonce and body hash, a constant-time compare, a five-minute skew window and a replay cache, with the key derived by HKDF from six spoken words and never written to a file.
674 manifest entries naming ten local generators with their full settings, a checker that exits non-zero on an uncovered file, and fonts built from stroke skeletons rather than downloaded.

Several tests read the source and fail the build on a pattern — the storage boundary, wall-clock animations inside captured regions, capture handles that await a route, modules naming their own paper. These are the cheapest possible guards against the specific regressions they name, and they are the reason the architecture has stayed coherent.
verdict: Structurally this holds up. There is one event log with one store behind it, the boundary is enforced by a test that fails the build rather than by a convention, eighteen event types are declared in one registry that the thread, the search index, the notification defaults and the paper assignment all read from, typing and presence are a separate wire type that two tests prove never reaches the log, read markers are folded into a projection field by a generic rule rather than a special case, the host will bind a tailnet address or refuse to start, nothing secret has ever been committed in 114 commits, every asset names a local generator, and 103 tests pass. That is most of what the rubric row asks for. What it does not yet have is the last mile of coherence in the two places where a per-type list escaped the registry's reach. The fifth shared-life module was added to the type registry, the renderer table, the paper assignment, the doc and the test map — and missed in app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:85, where its row now reads 'passed on', a registry id with the underscore taken out, in the one surface whose whole job is to name the kinds of event in a person's words. The same shape of gap has the app's entire furniture register — every tab, stamp, module label and margin note — set in Teo's handwriting, because pubspec.yaml:97 declares a DeskStamp family that points at TeoHand.ttf and the third face the build script names was never produced. Neither is blocking and neither is deep: one is a missing switch arm, the other a font that was specified and not built. But together they say the same thing about extensibility, which is that adding a kind of thing here is a directory and one line plus a checklist of six other files that only the tests half remember, and the two entries on that checklist without a test are the two that were forgotten.
